judge: python3 docs/lanes/bf2stall433/armread.py --a <A1> <A2> <A3> --b <B1> <B2> <B3> (rows from 45 s before mark gameplay to the end, as collapse433's tables; the script is committed with this file and is not edited after a run lands)
prediction: #433 lane.bf2stall433. Battlefield 2's heavy views (BE >= 1800 draws a frame) spend 35-40 ms of GPU time a frame at ~12-14 us per draw, a slope that did not shrink at 1.53x the GPU clock or in sysmem (docs/lanes/collapse433/NOTES.md section 7). Reading the renderer (docs/lanes/bf2stall433/NOTES.md sections 1-2): there is no per-draw barrier, event or render-pass split on master, but every draw's vertex fetch reads the per-frame FRAMEn_VERTEX_RAM buffers, which vk/buffer.c creates HOST_ACCESS_RANDOM. VMA then prefers HOST_CACHED, and on Turnip/KGSL the only cached type on ARM is IO-coherent, so every vertex fetch snoops the CPU caches. That latency belongs to the memory system, not the GPU core clock. B (57fe561924) copies only what was uploaded since the last finish into one device-local buffer, in the aux command buffer, and binds that buffer. If the snoop path is the per-draw cost, heavy-view GPU ms falls by a fifth or more and the per-draw slope with it. If GPU ms does not move, V is refuted as the cause and the per-draw constant reload (U, NOTES section 3) is next. Size if it holds: heavy views 35-40 ms -> under 30, so those windows reach 30 fps (currently 0 of 24 heavy windows at >= 29.5).

legs.M0 (instrument): Every run reaches 'mark gameplay' and has >= 15 rows (60-flip windows with hakuX-pace, hakuX-phase GPU and xemu-work BE) from 45 s before the mark to the end. A run without them is VOID, not zero (armread.py prints VOID), and is rerun once within the lane's 6-run budget, or the leg is reported on the runs that exist.
legs.P0 (premise, the counter in the binary): Every B run logs '[vtxmirror] on: ... host type N flags 0x.. cached=1 coherent=1 ...; mirror type M ... host_visible=0'. FAILS if the host copies are not cached-coherent: then there was no snoop to remove, and P1 is read as INERT, not as a refutation of V. A runs log no [vtxmirror] line (master).
legs.P1 (the per-draw cost, the number that c: Median GPU ms per frame over rows with BE >= 1800, pooled per arm: B/A <= 0.80 PASS; 0.80-0.95 PARTIAL (some of the cost, not most); > 0.95 FAIL: the IO-coherent vertex fetch is not the per-draw cost. For scale, two master runs with different views (collapse433's GMEM and sysmem soaks) read 0.946 on this ratio.
legs.P2 (slope): Least-squares GPU ms = a*BE + c over all rows per arm: a_B <= 0.75 * a_A (A is expected near collapse433's 0.0119).
legs.P3 (frame rate): Heavy-view median window fps B >= A + 2.0, or B's share of heavy windows at >= 29.5 fps exceeds A's by > 0.15. And over all rows (P3b) B's >= 29.5 share is not below A's by more than 0.05 (no regression).
legs.P4 (cost of the copy): Light views (BE < 1200): median GPU ms B <= A*1.05 + 0.5. Transfer GPU ms (phase X) median B <= A + 0.5. [vtxmirror] kb per 120 flips after the first two lines is read and reported; a full-range copy after startup (full= > 0 in mid-run lines) is reported as a finding.
legs.P5 (resolution): Each arm needs >= 8 rows with BE >= 1800. Fewer: P1-P3 are BELOW RESOLUTION, not failed.
legs.M1 (movement): frames_every 20: the frames of each run are read across the whole window and the report says whether the player moved (view changes, ammo/score moving). A run parked against a wall is reported as such; its rows still count, because the bins are by BE, but the report names it.
